name: Y Combinator
standard_terms: Standard deal, publicly documented on the YC site. Confirm current terms before applying.
fit_rationale: Broadest investor access of any programme, and the fastest route to a competitive seed round. Four batches a year means the timing cost of applying is low.
notes: Batch runs January to March in San Francisco with a three-day in-person kick-off. Late applications are still reviewed but without a guaranteed response time.

name: PearX
standard_terms: Confirm current terms on the Pear site.
fit_rationale: Pre-seed focused with hands-on partner involvement. Two cohorts a year, winter roughly January to April and summer roughly July to October.
notes: Runs an early deadline ahead of the regular one - applying early is usually worth it.

name: a16z Speedrun
standard_terms: Confirm current cheque and terms on the programme site.
fit_rationale: AI-native programme with a large standard cheque and direct access to a multistage firm that could lead the next round.
notes: Confirm the current cohort deadline - the cadence has changed between cycles.

standard_terms: No equity. Credits, hardware pricing and technical support.

name: Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub
standard_terms: No equity. Azure and OpenAI credits, tooling.
fit_rationale: Non-dilutive credits that meaningfully reduce burn during the raise.

name: AWS Activate
standard_terms: No equity. AWS credits and support.
fit_rationale: Non-dilutive credits. Larger tiers require a referral from an approved investor or accelerator.
notes: Rolling applications. The credit tier depends on who refers you - worth asking an investor for the referral.
